claims.claim: Fresh session with default_transaction_read_only=on: INSERT fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: On a disposable PostgreSQL 16, a non-superuser role with default_transaction_read_only=on could not INSERT in a fresh session (T1).
claims.public_wording: Fresh session, try an INSERT, and you get the error: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction.

claims.claim: SET default_transaction_read_only=off in-session restores writes
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: The same session, after SET default_transaction_read_only=off, completed the INSERT (T2).
claims.public_wording: SET default_transaction_read_only = off in the same session: the INSERT succeeds.

claims.claim: START TRANSACTION READ WRITE restores writes
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: An explicit READ WRITE transaction completed the INSERT (T3).
claims.public_wording: START TRANSACTION READ WRITE: the INSERT succeeds.

claims.claim: default_transaction_read_only is a USERSET parameter; any role can change it for its own session
claims.independent_support: T2 demonstrated a non-superuser role lifting it
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Per PostgreSQL 16 docs the parameter context is USERSET (settable by any role for its own session); T2 showed a non-superuser role doing so.
claims.public_wording: The parameter's context is USERSET, which means any role can change it for its own session — that is the documented behavior, not just our trial.

claims.claim: Superuser is bound by the default in a fresh session but bypasses it at will via SET
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: A superuser's fresh session honored the default (T9a); the same superuser lifted it with SET (T9b).
claims.public_wording: A superuser in a fresh session is bound by the default — the INSERT fails. Then the superuser runs SET and lifts it at will. We ran both trials.

claims.claim: Our retirement doc said the setting 'binds even superusers'
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: The retirement doc's text states the read-only enforcement 'binds even superusers' (K2).
claims.public_wording: Our own retirement doc said the setting 'binds even superusers.'

claims.claim: The doc framed its claim as scoped to the application's connection pattern; whether the app actually behaves that way is UNVERIFIED
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: The doc presents its claim as scoped to the app's connection pattern (K2); the app's actual behavior is unverified (U1/N1) and must not be asserted.
claims.primary_source: K2 record (doc's own scoping); U1 as the explicit non-claim
claims.public_wording: The doc framed the claim as scoped to our application's connection pattern — the doc's author's understanding was that the app never issues SET or START TRANSACTION. We have not verified that in the gateway code.
claims.scope: doc text only; app behavior out of scope (N1)

claims.claim: REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE blocks all attempted writes for a non-superuser role, including inside an explicit READ WRITE transaction
claims.counterevidence: none; SECURITY DEFINER / ownership paths are a different role's privilege, not the revoked role writing (C-F1 addressed)
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: After REVOKE of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, a non-superuser role could not write, even under explicit READ WRITE (T10). Scoped: the revoked role; not SECURITY DEFINER or ownership paths of other roles.
claims.public_wording: REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE on the table, from a non-superuser role. That blocked every write we attempted, including inside an explicitly requested READ WRITE transaction.
claims.scope: non-superuser role, PG 16, attempted write classes in T10

claims.claim: Superusers bypass permission checks; REVOKE cannot bind a superuser
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Per PostgreSQL docs, superusers bypass all permission checks; therefore REVOKE cannot bind a superuser. Cite as docs, not as our trial (N6).
claims.public_wording: Superusers bypass permission checks. That is documented PostgreSQL behavior — we did not trial it, we are citing the docs.

claims.claim: Our journal role (ping on ping-core-01) is a superuser
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Read-only inspection showed role ping on ping-core-01 is a superuser (C8).
claims.primary_source: read-only inspection of Oracle (ping-core-01), 2026-09-30; zero write attempts
claims.public_wording: And our own journal role is a superuser.

claims.claim: Honest seal description: session default verified present and active; app discipline unverified; append-only triggers verified present but untested
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: C8 verified the role setting and its presence in a fresh session; U1 (gateway code) is unverified; U2 (trigger blocking behavior) is untested. Do not compress to 'sealed' or 'unsealed' (N7).
claims.primary_source: C8 read-only inspection; U1/U2 as explicit non-claims
claims.public_wording: The session default is verified present in the role settings and active in a fresh session. The application discipline it depends on is unverified — we have not read the gateway code. The append-only triggers on the journal are verified present; we have not tested whether they actually block UPDATE and DELETE.
claims.scope: ping-core-01 as of 2026-09-30; tracks C8's residual-risk statement (N7)

claims.claim: CREATE TEMP TABLE fails inside a read-only transaction
claims.counterevidence: none; K1's overbroad secondary source contradicted and resolved
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: CREATE TEMP TABLE raised 'cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction' (T4).
claims.public_wording: CREATE TEMP TABLE inside a read-only transaction fails — we tried it.

claims.claim: INSERT and COPY FROM on an already-existing temp table succeed in a read-only transaction
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: DML (INSERT, COPY FROM) on existing temp tables succeeded read-only (T11); the docs' COPY exemption is worded around non-temporary tables.
claims.primary_source: disposable PG 16 trial T11, 2026-09-30; PG docs COPY exemption wording ('if the table they would write to is not a temporary table')
claims.public_wording: But INSERT and COPY FROM on a temp table that already exists succeed. The exemption is DML on existing temp tables, not DDL.
claims.scope: existing temp tables, DML only, PG 16

claims.claim: Advisory locks and LISTEN/NOTIFY function normally in read-only transactions
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: pg_advisory_lock/unlock and LISTEN/NOTIFY functioned normally in read-only transactions (T6/T7).
claims.public_wording: Advisory locks and LISTEN/NOTIFY work fine inside read-only transactions.

claims.claim: nextval() on a sequence is blocked in read-only transactions
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: SELECT nextval(seq) raised an error in a read-only transaction (T5).
claims.public_wording: nextval() on a sequence is blocked.

claims.claim: Trials ran on PG 16; the journal runs PG 17; docs indicate parity; not directly trialed
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Same as public wording (N3: one caveat line).
claims.public_wording: Our trials ran on PostgreSQL 16; the journal runs 17. The docs indicate parity; we did not trial it.

claims.claim: No pooler or proxy between gateway and database was inspected
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Same as public wording (N4).
claims.public_wording: We did not inspect any pooler or proxy between the gateway and the database.

claims.claim: Full extent of disk writes possible under read-only was not mapped beyond the tested operations
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Same as public wording (N5).
claims.public_wording: We did not map the full extent of what can be written to disk under read-only beyond the operations we tested.

claims.claim: Next research mission: test the append-only triggers on a disposable database (Oracle write attempts stay out of scope)
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Same as public wording. Do NOT run in this block (task constraint).
claims.public_wording: The next mission is already queued: test the triggers on a disposable database. No writes against the journal — that stays out of scope.

claims.claim: default_transaction_read_only is a session default, not a privilege boundary
claims.counterevidence: none admissible; A-F2 binds the scope
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: At the privilege layer, default_transaction_read_only is a session default, not a privilege boundary (T2/T3 + docs). While U1 is unresolved, this must not be extended to 'your system is unsealed' (A-F2/N1).
claims.public_wording: What we had was a session default, not a privilege boundary.
claims.scope: the privilege layer; scoped by A-F2 while U1 is unresolved (N1)

claims.claim: We are not claiming the journal is sealed; we are not claiming it is unsealed
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Same as public wording (N7: use C8's residual-risk statement verbatim; this is its prose form).
claims.public_wording: We are not claiming our journal is unsealed, and we are not claiming it is sealed. We are claiming exactly what we verified, and naming what we did not.

claims.claim: A secondary source overstated the temp-table exemption; trials corrected it to DML-only on existing temp tables
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: K1: prior belief + secondary source ('operations on temporary tables are permitted in read-only transactions') contradicted by T4; resolved as DML-only on existing temp tables (T11).
claims.primary_source: K1 contradiction record; T4 vs T11
claims.public_wording: A secondary source we read overstated this as a general temp-table exemption; the trials corrected it to the narrower truth.

claims.claim: The setting is a default the role can lift; the revocation is a boundary the role cannot cross (for non-superuser roles)
claims.maximum_defensible_wording: Interpretive summary of the demonstrated contrast; must always carry the non-superuser scope (CL-09) and must not be presented as a separate trial.
claims.primary_source: trial contrast, BLOCK-20-40-REPORT.md (C-F3: contribution is the demonstrated contrast)
claims.public_wording: The setting is a default the role can lift; the revocation is a boundary the role cannot cross.
claims.scope: non-superuser roles; explanatory framing of the T2/T3-vs-T10 contrast

candidates.H1: Your Postgres read-only seal is a default, not a boundary
candidates.H2: We sealed our journal with default_transaction_read_only. Then we checked what it actually seals.
candidates.H3: REVOKE beats read-only: the exact boundary of Postgres's read-only seal
